To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
antigenic stimulation in vitro with CMV-peptide and CMV-antibody, in combination with IL-2 or with IL-21, induced CCR7 expression on CMV-specific T-cells.
antigen-specific stimulation induces re-expression of CCCR7, CD62L and chemotactic migration in CMV-specific CD 8+ T cells.
CMV-specific T cells re-express CCCR7 upon antigenic stimulation in vitro and that these cells are able to migrate to a chemokine source in transwell assays.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CCR7 in the migration of human CMV-specific T cells.
the role of the chemokine system in the regulation of T-cell trafficking and function during CMV infection and latency.
the functional re-expression of the chemokine CCR7 on virus-specific T cells during the course of an infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CCR7 expression on virus-specific T cells is not fixed but can be modulated by the presence of antigen and specific cytokines.

antigen-specific stimulation of CMV-specific CD4(+) or CD8(+) cells induces the expression of CCR7, and that the expression of CCL19 and CCL21 in the vicinity of antigen-specific cells induces migration towards the chemokine gradient.
antigenic stimulation in vitro induces functional re-expression of the chemokine receptors CCR7 and CD62L on CMV-specific T cells, which allows migration towards specific chemokine gradients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
antigenic stimulation in vitro induced re-expression of chemokine receptors on CMV-specific T cells and restored the migratory capacity of the cells.
antigen-specific stimulation of CMV-specific cells induced functional expression of CCR7, which was dependent on the combination of cytokines and antigen.

antigen-specific stimulation induced functional re-expressions of CCR7, CD62L and the migratory capacity of CMV-specific CD(+) T cells which suggests that the functional properties of virus-activated CD8(+) effector T cells are flexible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chemokine receptors CCR7 and CCR5 can be re-expressed on CMV-specific T cells upon stimulation with the specific CM V-peptide and CMV-antigens.
CCR7 expression can be induced in CMV-specific T cells in vitro by antigen-specific stimulation in the presence of IL-2 and IL-21.
the migratory potential of CMV-specific CD 8+ T cells can be modulated by antigenic stimulation and that these cells can be recruited to lymph nodes by chemokines.
